resources.string: This mode requires a rooted device with a root manager that grants DFTB superuser access.
The diagnostics run itself failed unexpectedly. Re-run; if it persists, share the log from System overview.
The check did not finish in time. A pending superuser prompt or an unresponsive service is usually the cause; answer any prompt and re-run.
The check crashed before producing a result. The raw error is shown above.
DFTB must read and write the whole shared storage to back up files and to write archives. Grant \"All files access\" in the system settings page.
Not granted. The root shell can still read everything, but SAF-free browsing of shared storage will be unavailable.
On Android 10, reading and writing shared storage requires the storage runtime permission.
Not granted. The root shell can still read everything, but direct browsing of shared storage will be unavailable.
Without notifications a running backup cannot show progress or report a failure while the app is in the background.
No app handles the folder picker. Destinations on SD cards and USB drives cannot be selected on this device.
Long backups over slow connections may be killed by Doze. Exempting DFTB keeps scheduled and resumed jobs alive.
Less than 500 MB free. Temporary archives and the job journal live here; free some space before backing up.
Install Shizuku (or Sui) and start it via wireless debugging or root, then re-run.
Shizuku is installed but its service is not running. Open the Shizuku app and start it, then return here.
This Shizuku is older than version 11 and cannot be used. Update Shizuku.
Allow DFTB in the Shizuku prompt. If you chose \"Don\'t ask again\", re-enable it from the Shizuku app\'s authorized-apps list.
Shizuku is running as root; app data of every package is reachable.
Shizuku is running as the ADB shell user; some app data directories will be unreadable.
No su binary is visible to this app. KernelSU and APatch hide it until access is granted, so this alone is not a failure.
No Magisk, KernelSU or APatch manager was detected.
Open your root manager and allow superuser access for DFTB, then re-run.
Could not identify Magisk, KernelSU or APatch from the shell.
Not found on PATH. The copy bundled with DFTB will be used.
Not found. Entering the global mount namespace (advanced root mode) relies on it.
Superuser access was not granted, so the companion module could not be inspected.
Flash the DFTB companion module from your root manager and reboot.
The module is disabled or scheduled for removal. Re-enable it in your root manager and reboot.
Not on PATH. The module is installed but its files are not mounted yet; a reboot usually fixes this.
Created on the first boot after installing the module; scheduled and resumed backups record their state here.
The secure key that protects your saved credentials is gone, but encrypted entries remain on this device. They can no longer be decrypted; re-enter the affected credentials to recreate them.
